title: Local equations and generic DVR of a prime divisor on a regular scheme
statement: Let $X$ be an integral regular locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $D\hookrightarrow X$ be an integral closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] with generic point $\xi$ [def-sc-generic-point] such that $\dim\mathcal O_{X,\xi}=1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Its defining ideal $\mathcal I_D$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] is an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. For every $x\in D$, if $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $f\in A$ generates $\mathcal I_{D,x}$, then $f$ is a nonzero prime element (a nonunit such that $f\mid ab$ implies $f\mid a$ or $f\mid b$). The canonical generization map identifies $\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$ with $A_{(f)}$, the localization at the complement of the prime ideal $(f)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The ring $\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$ is a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], and the image of $f$ is a uniformizer.

source.place: Tags 0AGA (divisors-lemma-weil-divisor-is-cartier-UFD) and 0AG9 (divisors-lemma-integral-effective-Cartier-divisor-dvr), applied to regular local rings as in the final paragraph of Tag 0AGB (divisors-lemma-codim-1-part). The identification with A_(f) is explicit in the second paragraph of the proof of 0AGB.

proof.text: Fix $x\in D$. By [def-weil-regular-scheme] choose a Noetherian affine neighborhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $x$. Since $X$ is integral, $R$ is a domain by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. By [def-weil-closed-immersion] and [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], $D\cap U=\operatorname{Spec}(R/J)$ and $\mathcal I_D|_U=\widetilde J$. This open of the integral scheme $D$ is nonempty, so $R/J$ is a domain and $J$ is prime. Its zero prime corresponds to $\xi$: the generic point belongs to every nonempty open, since its closure is $D$ [def-sc-generic-point]. Write $\mathfrak q\supseteq J$ for $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization], $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}=R_{\mathfrak q}$, $\mathcal I_{D,x}=JR_{\mathfrak q}=:\mathfrak p$, and $\mathcal O_{X,\xi}=R_J$. The last ideal $\mathfrak p$ is prime: $A/\mathfrak p=(R/J)_{\mathfrak q/J}$, a nonzero domain, by the fraction formulas.

source.place: Tag 0AGA (lemma-weil-divisor-is-cartier-UFD), proof opening; affine stalk descriptions in Schemes Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves).

proof.text: The generization homomorphism $A=R_{\mathfrak q}\to R_J$ sends $a/s$ to $a/s$. The complement of $\mathfrak p=JR_{\mathfrak q}$ consists precisely of fractions $b/t$ with $b\notin J$. Consequently [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] gives an isomorphism $A_{\mathfrak p}\to R_J$ by $(a/s)/(b/t)\mapsto at/(sb)$, with inverse $a/b\mapsto(a/1)/(b/1)$. All denominators displayed avoid the relevant prime; the fraction equality relation verifies that the formulas are well defined and inverse. Both maps agree with the germ maps on $R$, so this identifies the canonical generization map, rather than an arbitrary ring isomorphism. In particular $\dim A_{\mathfrak p}=1$.

source.place: Tag 0AGA, prime corresponding to the generic point; Tag 0AGB (lemma-codim-1-part), second proof paragraph: the generic local ring is A_(f).

proof.text: The ring $A$ is a domain: a product of two fractions over the domain $R$ is zero only if one numerator is zero. Prime ideals of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ correspond to prime ideals $P\subseteq\mathfrak p$ of $A$: extension consists of fractions with numerator in $P$, and contraction recovers $P$, since denominators lie outside $\mathfrak p$, hence outside $P$. These operations preserve strict inclusions. Thus $\dim A_{\mathfrak p}=1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] says that $\mathfrak p\ne0$ (otherwise $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is the fraction field) and no prime lies strictly between $0$ and $\mathfrak p$. This is the height-one condition in [lem-trf-ufd-height-one].

source.place: Tag 0AGA, proof: dimension one of A_p means p has height one.

proof.text: By [def-weil-regular-scheme], $A$ is regular local and Noetherian. Choose generators of its maximal ideal of length $\dim A$, a regular system of parameters by [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Apply [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization] with the empty selected sublist ($r=0$) to obtain that $A$ is a unique factorization domain. Since $\mathfrak p$ is a height-one prime, [lem-trf-ufd-height-one] yields $\mathfrak p=(f)$ for some $f\in A$. This $f$ is nonzero, because $\mathfrak p\ne0$, and is a nonunit, because $\mathfrak p$ is proper. If $f\mid ab$, then $ab\in\mathfrak p$, hence $a\in\mathfrak p$ or $b\in\mathfrak p$; equivalently $f\mid a$ or $f\mid b$.

source.place: Tag 0AGA, proof using height-one primes in a UFD; final paragraph of Tag 0AGB invokes More on Algebra Tag 0AG0 (lemma-regular-local-UFD).

proof.text: Repeat Step 5 at each $x\in D$. For $y\in X\setminus D$, take an affine open neighborhood contained in $X\setminus D$; there the ideal is the whole structure sheaf, generated by the nonzerodivisor $1$, since its quotient defines the empty closed subscheme [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Together these neighborhoods form an open cover on which $\mathcal I_D$ is generated by a nonzerodivisor. This is exactly an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal].

source.place: Tag 0AG8, conclusion of (2), and Tag 0AGA, final sentence.

proof.text: For the arbitrary generator in the statement, let $g\in A$ satisfy $(g)=\mathcal I_{D,x}=\mathfrak p$. The same direct argument as in Step 4 shows that $g\ne0$, $g$ is a nonunit, and $g\mid ab$ implies $g\mid a$ or $g\mid b$, since $\mathfrak p$ is a proper nonzero prime ideal. Step 2 now reads $\mathcal O_{X,\xi}=A_{(g)}$ through the canonical generization map. Its maximal ideal is $(g)A_{(g)}$ by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Thus the conclusion holds for every generator, not only the one selected in Step 4.

source.place: Tag 0AGB, second proof paragraph, local equations f_i and the identification O_i=A_(f_i).

proof.text: Finally $\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$ is regular local by [def-weil-regular-scheme], and has dimension one by hypothesis. Apply [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr] to conclude that it is a discrete valuation ring. Step 7 identifies its maximal ideal with the ideal generated by the image of every chosen local equation $g$. By the definition of uniformizer in [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], that image is a uniformizer. This also applies at $x=\xi$; no global Noetherian or dimension bound on $X$ was used.
